summary: g=f0_prime, including A/(|v|^3+vt^3) cutoff jump masses for Fn=4.

capability: g=f0_prime, including A/(|v|^3+vt^3) cutoff jump masses for Fn=4.
operation: evaluate the equilibrium distribution derivative and cutoff jumps
equilibrium controls -> f0'(v) and cutoff jump masses
discovery.model: Linear one-dimensional single-spatial-Fourier-mode electrons, fixed ions.
discovery.geometry: One velocity coordinate and one spatial Fourier mode.
discovery.boundary: One-dimensional finite velocity grid; Fn selects fixed equilibria; weak Fn4 cutoff requires a uniform grid; no time evolution.

identity.relation: g=f0_prime, including A/(|v|^3+vt^3) cutoff jump masses for Fn=4.
identity.definition: g=f0_prime, including A/(|v|^3+vt^3) cutoff jump masses for Fn=4.
identity.model: Linear one-dimensional single-spatial-Fourier-mode electrons, fixed ions.
identity.geometry: One velocity coordinate and one spatial Fourier mode.
identity.boundary: One-dimensional finite velocity grid; Fn selects fixed equilibria; weak Fn4 cutoff requires a uniform grid; no time evolution.
assumptions: Velocity-window truncation and recurrence are separate from temporal integration error.

inputs.name: vv
inputs.constraints: Finite one-dimensional; aligned with df and df0dv when applicable.

inputs.name: Fn
inputs.description: Built-in equilibrium, unit density: 1 Maxwellian exp(-v^2/2)/sqrt(2pi) (unit variance); 2 kappa Gamma(kappa)/(Gamma(kappa-1/2) sqrt(2 pi kappa)) (1+v^2/(2 kappa))^-kappa, i.e. theta^2=2 with variance 2kappa/(2kappa-3), NOT unit temperature; 3 triangle max(0,1-|v|); 4 cutoff slowing-down.

inputs.name: k
inputs.description: Spatial Fourier wavenumber in inverse Debye length.

inputs.name: kappa
inputs.description: Kappa index of the Fn=2 family. The family is not rescaled to unit variance; for a kappa distribution at a prescribed temperature pass its derivative as df0dv to vp_init.

inputs.name: cutoff_mode
inputs.description: Fn4 weak derivative or explicit source smooth-only forcing.
inputs.constraints: weak or smooth; weak Fn4 requires increasing uniform grid.

outputs.name: result
outputs.description: Tuple (g,wr,wi): g [N], theoretical wr=1 and wi=-k sqrt(2) only for Fn=2,kappa=1; otherwise theory is None.
outputs.shape: As described in output mapping or tuple.
outputs.constraints: Tuple of finite derivative and optional theoretical frequencies; no hidden state.

preconditions: vv is a finite one-dimensional real array.
k is finite and positive; Fn, kappa and cutoff_mode select a supported branch.
supported: Fn=1,2,3 and Fn=4 with weak or smooth cutoff derivative.
excluded: This leaf returns a derivative and optional theory frequencies; it does not evolve a state.

failure_semantics.invalid_input: ValueError for unsupported Fn/cutoff_mode, nonfinite or non-vector vv, invalid kappa, invalid k or a non-increasing/nonuniform weak-cutoff grid.
failure_semantics.runtime_failure: FloatingPointError when the derivative is not finite.
failure_semantics.nonconvergence: Not applicable; no iterative solve is performed.
failure_semantics.partial_results: No mapping is returned after an exception.

example.code:
from scirel.kinetic.vlasov_poisson import vp_distribution
import numpy as np
g,wr,wi=vp_distribution(np.linspace(-6,6,101),4)
assert g.shape == (101,)
example.description: Evaluate the Fn=4 weak cutoff derivative on a 101-point velocity grid.
example.expected: PASS: .venv/bin/python completed; g has shape (101,) and the weak-cutoff branch is finite.

scope: Discrete Poisson constraint and off-diagonal rank-one feedback.
Dense matrix-exponential RK4 order; analytic free-streaming and damped-cosine diagnostics.
Slowing-down weak derivative integration-by-parts and default 2049-node/2000-step execution.
verification.evidence_ceiling: Independent semidiscrete mathematical and selected scenario regressions; actual run/installed-wheel receipts are recorded separately, not inferred from test existence.
known_limitations: Finite-window rectangle rule and sampling recurrence TR=2pi/(k*dv).
Fn4 truncated density retains original coefficient and is not renormalized after cutoff.
Peak diagnostic assumes standing oscillation; rotating complex exponential has no amplitude peaks.
